task.description: Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0262-20260822/step-01-issue-fixer.json's result.summary in full -- it is ISSUE-FIXER's complete diagnosis and recommendation for ISS-0262 (GH#510). Design a fix per its recommendation: broaden handoff_files/0's discovery beyond the hardcoded `handoffs/**/*.json` glob, and add a new hard check (ISSUE-FIXER suggests naming it H6) that flags any handoff-shaped file under handoffs/<run_id>/ that is NOT valid JSON (or does not carry the expected .json extension) as a violation, gating the exit code the same way H1-H4 do. Design must state precisely: (a) the new discovery glob/pattern, distinguishing a handoff-shaped file from incidental non-handoff files that might live under handoffs/ (e.g. registry.json and orchestrator.log themselves must stay excluded -- check how @registry_file is already excluded and preserve that plus exclude orchestrator.log by the same mechanism); (b) the H6 check's exact classification logic (three outcomes per ISSUE-FIXER: .json+valid -> existing path, .json+invalid -> existing PARSE path, non-.json extension -> new H6 violation) as @spec-style signatures/pseudocode, not implementation bodies; (c) the exact disposition for the 10 (not 9 -- ISSUE-FIXER corrected the original count) pre-existing Markdown files under handoffs/WF03-ISS0258-20260822/ -- ISSUE-FIXER recommends grandfathering them individually by exact path mirroring the existing @grandfathered list pattern (rule tag "H6", one entry per file), not converting them to JSON; state the exact 10 file paths to grandfather (list them, do not just say 'the 10 files' -- verify the count and names yourself against the actual directory rather than trusting the diagnosis's number). Also design the test fixture requirement: a real non-JSON handoff-shaped fixture file TEST-DESIGNER will use to prove H6 catches a violation (e.g. under a throwaway test-only handoffs-shaped directory or an in-repo fixture path -- decide and specify exactly where it lives and what it's named). No implementation code -- signatures, data shapes, and the grandfather-list additions as data, not function bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc under lib/letflow/design/ (or a suitable location per this project's design-artefact convention) covers: new discovery mechanism, H6 check logic and violation message shape, exact grandfather-list additions (all real file paths, verified against disk, not assumed count), and the test fixture's exact location/shape
No .ex implementation function bodies present -- signatures and pseudocode only
Design explicitly addresses backward compatibility: existing grandfathered H1-H4 entries and existing valid .json handoffs must not newly violate H6
Design states how orchestrator.log and registry.json remain excluded from H6's scope

result.summary: Design written to lib/letflow/design/iss0262-lint-handoffs-non-json-discovery.md. Re-verified ISSUE-FIXER's diagnosis first-hand (handoff_files/0 at lint_handoffs.ex:186-191 globs only **/*.json) and re-measured the WF03-ISS0258-20260822 directory myself: exactly 10 .md files, matching ISSUE-FIXER's corrected count. Found and corrected a flaw in ISSUE-FIXER's literal suggested glob (**/step-*.*): 14 existing, currently-linted .json files under WF02-REQ018/019/021 are named without a hyphen (step00-git-setup.json, step01-code-design.json, ...); a hyphen-requiring glob would have stopped discovering them -- a regression. Design instead classifies a 'handoff-shaped' file as any basename starting with the literal 'step' (Path.wildcard(Path.join(dir, "**/step*.*"))), which covers both naming styles and, measured against the real handoffs/ tree, naturally excludes registry.json, orchestrator.log, escalations.yaml, one redraft-*.md file and three *-verdict.md files -- none of their basenames start with 'step' -- with @registry_file's reject kept as stated defense-in-depth. handoff_files/0 becomes handoff_files/1 with a default arg (dir \\ @handoffs_dir) so TEST-DESIGNER can point discovery at an isolated fixture tree without ever touching or mutating the real handoffs/ corpus. H6 classification (handoff_kind/1, pure, extension-only, content never consulted) gives exactly the three outcomes ISSUE-FIXER specified: .json+decodes -> existing H1-H4 path unchanged; .json+decode fails -> existing PARSE path unchanged; non-.json (any content) -> new H6, hard/gating, reusing the existing violation map and grandfather-tuple shape verbatim. All 10 WF03-ISS0258-20260822 .md paths are individually grandfathered under rule tag "H6" (exact paths listed in the design's SS3.1, verified against Glob output this session, not assumed) so the fix does not turn today's green build red; a stated second-order consequence is that WF03-ISS0258-20260822 will newly appear in H5's (advisory-only, non-gating) missing_from_registry report, which is correct and intentional. Test fixture: a real, permanent, committed file at test/fixtures/lint_handoffs/h6/step-01-fixture-non-json.md, outside handoffs/ entirely, exercised directly via handoff_files/1 (proves discovery) and lint_file/2 (proves H6 classification and violation shape) so TEST-DESIGNER never needs a temp dir or touches the grandfather list. Backward compatibility (existing grandfathered H1-H3 entries, existing valid .json handoffs, orchestrator.log/registry.json exclusion) stated explicitly in SS5 and SS1.1's classification table. No implementation code -- @spec signatures, one glob pattern, pseudocode case shapes, and grandfather-list data only.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to gate this design before ELIXIR-DEV implements it.
